engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Opening: Sicilian Defence Basics
chess.body: After 1.e4 c5 — Black fights for the centre asymmetrically. Black gets queenside counterplay; White gets kingside attack. Most common openings at club level. Learn one variation: Sicilian Najdorf (1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 a6). It's played by Kasparov, Fischer, Carlsen. Understand the plans before memorising moves.

wisdom.title: The Gratitude Practise
wisdom.body: Every morning, before checking your phone: name 3 specific things you're grateful for. Not 'health and family' — that's lazy. Something specific: 'my daughter smiled when she saw me yesterday,' 'I understood a balance sheet faster than last year,' 'KL at 26°C.' Specificity trains the brain to notice abundance.

book.author: Andy Grove
book.lesson: Grove invented OKRs at Intel in the 1970s. John Doerr brought them to Google in 1999. The structure: Objective (qualitative, inspirational — where do we want to go?) + Key Results (quantitative, measurable — how will we know we got there?). Rules: 3-5 OKRs per quarter. Each with 3-5 key results. They should be set at 60-70% achievable — if you always hit 100%, your targets are too easy. OKRs should be public so every team member can see how their work connects to company goals. The discipline of writing OKRs forces clarity on what actually matters and exposes misalignment between teams.
book.key_quote: What gets measured gets managed. What gets publicly committed to gets done.
book.action: Write one personal OKR for this quarter: Objective (where you want to be in your career by end of Q3) + 3 Key Results (how you'll know you got there).
crux: A manager's output is the output of their organisation plus the organisations they influence.
Managerial leverage = output ÷ time spent. Optimise for leverage, not effort.
Highest-leverage activities: training, and setting direction that many people then act on.
Production has three constraints everywhere: quality, cost, delivery time.
Inspect at the earliest, cheapest stage. Fixing at the end costs orders of magnitude more.
Indicators must come in pairs — one for output, one for the quality you might sacrifice for it.
Meetings are the medium of managerial work. A bad meeting is a process failure, not a waste of time in general.
One-on-ones are the highest-leverage meeting. The subordinate sets the agenda.
Decisions should be made at the lowest level with both knowledge and responsibility.
Aim for peer decision-making, then clear commitment even from dissenters.
Task-relevant maturity determines management style: low TRM needs structure, high TRM needs delegation.
Performance reviews exist to improve performance, not to rank people.
Three motivators when money is sufficient: competence, achievement, and self-actualisation.
learnings: Leverage is the only useful lens on how a manager spends an hour.
Paired indicators stop you optimising one number into a disaster.
Training your team is not overhead. It is the highest-return activity available.
Catch problems at the cheapest stage — the value-add curve is brutal.
examples: Grove's breakfast-factory model teaches limiting-step scheduling, quality gates, and capacity planning with eggs and toast.
Intel's move out of memory into microprocessors was executed through middle managers reallocating capacity before senior leadership formally decided.
Grove taught a class himself for years — one lecture, hundreds of managers, permanent leverage.
adapt: FP&A leverage: build the model once so 20 people read it right, instead of answering 20 questions.
Pair every metric: signals sent AND measured expectancy. One alone produced 180 alerts.
Inspect early — type-check and lint before commit, not after deploy.
In the Dubai role, one-on-ones with the business owners will be the highest-leverage hour of the week.

minimalism.title: Owning Is A Liability
minimalism.body: Every object requires storage, maintenance, insurance, cleaning, moving, and eventual disposal. The purchase price is the smallest number in that list. Accountants of all people should price the full cost.
minimalism.action: Before the next purchase, write the 5-year total cost of ownership.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Handle The Bill Without Theatre
etiquette.body: Decide before you arrive. Settle it quietly. The public wrestle over a bill embarrasses everyone at the table.
etiquette.action: Settle the next bill before it reaches the table.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: Keep A Line A Day
stillness.body: One sentence about the day. Not a journal habit that collapses in a week — one line. In ten years it becomes the only accurate record of your life that exists.
stillness.action: Write one line tonight. Date it.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Base Rates
model.body: Before believing your case is special, ask what usually happens. Most restaurants fail. Most projects overrun. Most traders lose. Your plan starts from that number, not from zero.
model.action: Find the base rate for your current bet before adjusting for your edge.
model.label: Mental Model

arabic.use: A warm thank-you with more weight than shukran. Good for someone senior.
arabic.label: Arabic

drill.title: The Five Whys
drill.body: Ask why five times to get from symptom to cause. Most analysis stops at why one and fixes a symptom, which guarantees the problem returns.
drill.action: Take one recurring problem. Ask why five times. Write each answer.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: Light Sets The Clock
health.body: Morning daylight within an hour of waking anchors circadian rhythm and improves sleep that night more reliably than any supplement. Outdoor light is 10–100x brighter than indoor, even when overcast.
health.action: Ten minutes outside within an hour of waking. No sunglasses.
health.label: Health

quote.name: Steve Jobs
quote.quote: Quality is more important than quantity. One home run is much better than two doubles.

lesson.lesson: Concentrate all your thoughts upon the work at hand. The sun's rays do not burn until brought to a focus.

case.title: Xiaomi: Selling Phones Like Software
case.story: Xiaomi released phones at cost, made money on software and services. 5% net margin on hardware, 40%+ on MIUI ecosystem. $35B valuation in 5 years.
case.lesson: The product can be the distribution channel. Give away the razor, sell the blades.

fpna.title: Rolling Forecast
fpna.body: Rolling 12-month forecasts beat static annual budgets. Less time defending, more time deciding.

cfo.title: CFO Step 4: Board Communication
cfo.body: CFOs present to the Board. Boards want: Are we on budget? What's the cash position? What risks keep you up at night? Practice speaking to non-finance people. Remove jargon. Lead with the conclusion, not the workings.

money_hack.title: Gold via SGB
money_hack.body: Sovereign Gold Bonds: 2.5% interest + gold price appreciation. No storage cost.

dubai.title: Corporate tax changed the job
dubai.body: The UAE introduced 9% corporate tax from June 2023. Every group now needs someone who can model an effective tax rate, handle transfer pricing between free-zone and mainland entities, and file. That is new demand, and the supply of people who have actually done it is thin.
dubai.targets: Free-zone qualifying income at 0% is the question that separates the prepared from the rest.
dubai.action: Read the FTA corporate tax guide. Two hours buys you a whole interview answer.

desk.productivity: End every meeting with: who does what by when. No action = no meeting.

father.title: Offer food she can hold
father.do: Soft strips she can grip herself — steamed carrot, banana, well-cooked pasta. Accept the mess.
father.why: Self-feeding at 7 months develops the pincer grip and, more importantly, lets her control intake. Children who regulate their own portions early are less likely to over-eat later.

father.title: Protect the sleep routine
father.do: Same order, same lighting, same time — bath, feed, book, bed. Do it yourself at least twice a week.
father.why: Consistency of sequence matters more than the exact timing. Fathers who own bedtime regularly build a distinct attachment relationship rather than a substitute one.

life_wisdom.translation: Non-violence in thought, word and act
life_wisdom.teaching: The most demanding version is not physical — it is refusing to injure with speech or intent, including toward yourself.
life_wisdom.apply: Notice the sentence you would not say to a colleague, then check whether you say it to yourself about your own work. The standard should be the same.

life_wisdom.teaching: The Buddha's image: struck by an arrow, most people fire a second one into themselves — the story about what the first arrow means.
life_wisdom.apply: A stopped-out trade is the first arrow. 'I am bad at this' is the second. Only one of them was caused by the market.

speaking.title: Land the number
speaking.drill: Say five figures out loud with a small pause before each one: 'margin fell … 180 basis points'.
speaking.why: The pause makes the listener wait for the number, which makes them remember it.

interview_tech.q: Explain covenant headroom and how you monitor it.
interview_tech.a: Covenants are contractual ratios — typically net debt to EBITDA, interest cover, and sometimes minimum net worth — tested quarterly. Headroom is the distance between your forecast ratio and the limit. Monitor it forward, not backward: run the covenant calculation inside the rolling forecast so you see a breach two quarters out while you can still act. Post-IFRS 16, check whether the definitions are frozen GAAP or current GAAP — lease liabilities entering net debt has breached covenants that had nothing to do with performance.

interview_tech.q: What controls matter most in a 60-store retail environment?
interview_tech.a: Rank by exposure. Cash and tender reconciliation daily at store level with independent review; goods receiving matched three-way to purchase order and invoice, because that is where margin leaks; inventory counts on a rolling cycle rather than one annual heroic count; markdown authorisation limits by role; and user access in the ERP reviewed quarterly, especially for leavers. Segregation of duties is hardest at small stores — compensate with detective controls and exception reporting rather than pretending it exists.

interview_soft.a: They are screening for whether you have thought about it or are just leaving somewhere. Be concrete: the Gulf retail market's scale and the concentration of regional HQs; UAE corporate tax making the finance function genuinely more technical than it was; and the specific fit between your multi-country consolidation experience and a group operating across GCC markets. Do not lead with tax-free income or lifestyle — every candidate says it and none of it is about the job.

interview_soft.q: How do you prioritise when everything is urgent?
interview_soft.a: Give a working rule, not a philosophy. Something like: anything with a statutory deadline is non-negotiable; then anything that changes a decision being made this week; then anything that compounds — process fixes that stop the same fire recurring; then everything else. The part interviewers actually want: what you stopped doing and who you told. Prioritisation without explicit de-prioritisation is just a longer list.
